messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Convex geometry / affine-regular polygon stacking with explicit overlap proofs

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration of 13 points in the unit square maximizing the minimum triangle area is achieved by placing 12 points at the vertices of an affine-regular hexagonal grid (two interleaved equilateral triangular lattices, affinely stretched to fill the square boundary) plus one point at the center, yielding a minimum triangle area of 1/72. The proof that no smaller triangle arises follows from the affine-regular structure: every triangle is an affine image of a lattice triangle with integer area at least 1, scaled by the determinant factor 1/72, and the boundary overlap is controlled by the explicit affine map sending the regular hexagonal fundamental domain to the unit square."}
